declared.title: The motivating function of thinking about the future: Expectations versus fantasies.
declared.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
declared.foundIn: scout notes on Manson's ideas (idea 3); Crossref search « Oettingen Mayer motivating function of thinking about the future expectations versus fantasies » (2026-11-23)

population: 4 prospective samples: job-seeking graduates, students with a crush, students before an exam, hip-replacement patients

findings.text: Positive fantasies about a desired future predicted less effort and poorer performance weeks to 2 years later; positive expectations predicted the opposite

support.sentence: Positive expectations (judging a desired future as likely) predicted high effort and successful performance, but the reverse was true for positive fantasies (experiencing one's thoughts and mental images about a desired future positively).

limits: correlational: fantasies were measured, not manipulated; effort and performance followed weeks to 2 years later
one laboratory, 4 specific groups; sample sizes and countries not given in the abstract
fantasies scored by a semi-projective scenario measure, not everyday daydreams as in the book
no sample from the Middle East or North Africa
allegiance: Oettingen developed fantasy realization theory and mental contrasting (WOOP), which she also promotes
